newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end lower, hit by U.S. rate fears.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end lower, hit by U.S. rate fears.

text.p: 1522 GMT - UK gilts partly made back early losses and settled just 3/32 down on day. Gilts failed to respond to better than forecast UK RPI data in the morning, then fell further in afternoon after robust U.S. prices data. U.S likely to stay key focus Friday * June gilt futures settled at 114-14, down 3/32
"The market looks very tired and its failure to respond to the inflation data is a very bad sign," said one snior salesman.
"The news this week has almost all been good, but the market has just gone sideways. There is likley to be a bit of profittaking ahead."
Headline inflation fell to 2.4 percent in April from 2.6 percent in March while the underlying rate fell to 2.5 percent -- hitting the government's target -- from 2.7 percent in March.
Gilts edged lower after the data and slipped further down after U.S. core CPI came in above expectations and weekly jobless claims fell sharply.

"That made the market very concerned about the FOMC meeting but it seemed to calm down a bit after the Philly Fed report and production numbers," said a trader at a GEMM. "On balance I think the market thinks the Fed will not move next week."
With the FOMC meeting on May 20, the U.S. is likely to stay the focus for gilts on Friday and early next week.
"There is nothing of much interest out tomorrow so it could be a thin day and quite volatile," said the trader.
Short sterling had a better day than gilts and most contracts gained ground. June settled unchanged at 93.48, but September was up 0.02 at 93.27 and December up 0.02 at 93.10.

"There is a growing feeling that even though the Bank (of England) wants to raise rates as soon as possible it will hold off until after the budget, which may mean not moving until July," said the trader.
No dates have been set yet for the budget or the first meeting of the new Monetary Policy Committee has been set, but there is much speculation that the budget will be delivered on June 10.
